newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN Assembly pushes resolution on council reform.
newsitem.headline: UN Assembly pushes resolution on council reform.

text.p: The president of the U.N. General Assembly on Thursday presented a key resolution to enlarge the Security Council that would allow Japan and Germany to become permanent but without veto power.

The document from Razali Ismail of Malaysia would expand the 15-member council to 24 seats, and is considered the first serious attempt at concrete steps to reform the body after years of discussions. It envisages stages that would take about a year before final decisions are made and voted on by the assembly and the council.
Five countries -- the United States, Britain, France, China and Russia -- are permanent members with veto powers.

Razali's proposal would add five permanent members and four rotating non-permanent members. Two of the permanent members would be from industrialized states, and one each from Africa, Asia and Latin America. The four non-permanent members would be from Africa, Asia, Eastern Europe and Latin America.
But none of the new members would have veto power, a provision Japan and Germany are bound to oppose.

Italy's ambasador Paulo Fulci said Razali's proposals would make the council less democratic, creating three instead of two categories of members in a system "we shall not accept." British Ambassador Sir John Weston said it was a good basis for negotiation and should lead to a decision by the assembly.
